method: One ordinary-O3 executable runs 100 and 10,000 iterations of eight recoverable failures. Complete stdout matches CPython. DHAT replaces allocation routines and reports requested heap, not RSS; instruction-based lifetimes and instrumented durations are not speed results. Complete traces are embedded with repository/tool-cache paths normalized; counters are unchanged.

input_record.derivation: Start from dedented ACCEPTED['partial_construction']; replace the sole range(100) loop with an input-driven iterations local and range(iterations); replace the fixed success text with recovered plus the actual iteration count. The same generated binary is used for both inputs.

conclusion: Both runs peak at 18,140 requested bytes in 14 blocks and end with 17,408 bytes in 3 persistent I/O buffers. Allocation traffic grows with work while measured live heap remains bounded; this is evidence for these recovery paths, not a general leak-freedom proof.
